text.p: Trade was quiet on commodity markets overnight with U.S. markets closed for the President's Day holiday.
However in London copper prices rose $21 a tonne on short covering and gold firmed slightly. Oil trade was quiet as many traders were off at a conference, with prices firming slightly.
Base metals prices ended firmer across the board on Monday afternoon, led by an eleventh-hour spurt in copper.
Trading on the London Metal Exchange (LME) was dulled by New York's absence due to the U.S. President's Day holiday. Third Wednesday pricing passed routinely.

But copper popped up from lows around $2,250 per tonne in the morning, and then managed to pushed higher on short covering towards the end of the afternoon kerb. Three months copper ended the kerb at $2,278, up $21 from Friday's kerb close.
Aluminium crept higher with copper, ending at near its day's highs at $1,570 versus $1,564 on Friday.
But resistance at that level and then at $1,580 was likely to prove difficult for aluminium ,traders said.
Zinc was up by $5.00 at $1,215, boosted by an expected stocks fall on Tuesday.
Nickel traded in a very tight range and ended just $10 higher at $7,750.
U.S. wheat futures markets were closed for President's Day holiday.

London gold prices drifted slightly higher in quiet trade on Monday reflecting New York being closed for the President's Day holiday. Gold was fixed at $344.10 per ounce after $343.60 in the morning and $342.40 on Friday afternoon.

Gold has managed a sizeable bounce from its 3-3/4 year low of $336.90 posted last Wednesday. Even so, dealers were wary of saying gold had shaken off the bear trend which had pressured prices since the beginning of the year.

NYMEX was closed on Monday, but IPE Brent crude ended weak after a shortened session on Monday, under pressure from sloppy physical market fundamentals in Northwest Europe, dealers said. April Brent closed 13 cents lower at $20.36 a barrel, at the bottom of an 18-cent range posted in extremely light volume as many traders left their desks for industry functions on the first day of Institute of Petroleum Week.
Interest was also subdued during the afternoon by the absence of U.S. dealing thanks to the President's Day holiday.
